newsitem.title: USA: Iomega to cut staff, take $10 mln charge.
newsitem.headline: Iomega to cut staff, take $10 mln charge.

text.p: Iomega Corp said it plans to increase production at its Penang, Malaysia plant and relocate its European headquarters, which will result in staff cuts at its Roy, Utah plants and a $10 million fourth quarter charge.
Iomega said its Penang operations have reached volume production faster than expected, and are now equipped to produce all types of Iomega's personal storage products.

As a result, Iomega said that it will eliminate between 500 to 700 positions at its Roy facilities in the production, manufacturing and distribution areas, beginning in March. It expects a one-time charge of $10 million in the fourth quarter.
Iomega said that affected employees will be offered outplacement services through a career transition center located at an Iomega facility, medical benefit extensions and severance packages.

"Moving manufacturing operations to Penang gets us closer to our storage component suppliers, ultimately lowering the cost of handling and shipping inventory," said Wayne Stewart, chief operating officer, in a statement. "This strategy will benefit our customers by driving product costs down."
Iomega said it plans to transition manufacturing facilities at Roy to Penang throughout the first half 1997.

The Utah facility will remain the worldwide headquarters for Iomega and it will house research and development, strategic procurement, finance and accounting, administration, sales and marketing and distribution areas, beginning in March, 1997.

Iomega also said that in order to improve responsiveness to customers in Europe, Iomega also plans in early 1997 to move its European management and sales and marketing functions, to Geneva, Switzerland, and its European logistics and distribution function to Utrecht, the Netherlands.
